sermon.title: Return to Good Government
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer shows God punishing Babylon after using it to correct Judah: the writing on the wall, Belshazzar’s fall and Cyrus, named a century before birth, sending the Jews home. Daniel understood the seventy years by the books and prayed, confessing his and his fathers’ sins, as Leviticus 26 and 2 Chronicles 7:14 require. Through Christ we are freed from the law of sin and death and joined to him.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Points to check: Jeremiah 29:10 spoken as “29 9”; Leviticus 26:33 spoken as “verse 43”; 1 John 1:9 spoken as “John 19”; “70 weeks” for 70 years; 490 years from Saul’s kingship to the captivity; Babylon walls height; Cyrus Cylinder wording (“the most high God told me”); Cyrus 100 years before birth; Darius named as the one who slew Belshazzar. Sensitive content kept as spoken: Bush Sr. and Clinton/Ross Perot; secular humanism and progressive socialism; phony miracles and prophecies; prosperity preachers; Jesus-coming predictions; the poor working for welfare; divorce/remarriage when an unbeliever departs.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Or do you not know, brethren (for I speak to those who know the law), that the law has dominion over a man as long as he lives? For the woman who has a husband is bound by the law to her husband as long as he lives. But if the husband dies, she is released from the law of her husband. So then if, while her husband lives, she marries another man, she will be called an adulteress; but if her husband dies, she is free from that law, so that she is no adulteress, though she has married another man. Therefore, my brethren, you also have become dead to the law through the body of Christ, that you may be married to another—to Him who was raised from the dead, that we should bear fruit to God.

faqs.question: Is ancient Babylon still desolate?
faqs.answer: He says it is to this day.

faqs.question: How does he test a major prophecy?
faqs.answer: He looks for the confirming sign; no sign, no attention.

faqs.question: Who did God call his anointed shepherd?
Why were they captive seventy years?
faqs.answer: One year for each neglected Sabbath year.

faqs.question: Is any sin too hard for God to forgive?
When is the time to be saved?
faqs.answer: The moment you hear the message.
